```js
const ids = ['6:7','6:23','48:43','48:54','6:269','6:270','6:271','6:272','6:273','6:274','6:275','6:276','6:277','6:278','6:279','6:280','6:281','6:282','6:283','6:284','6:285','5:17','5:22','5:27','5:37','5:42','5:47','5:55','5:60','5:65','5:70','5:78','5:83'];
const out = [];
for (const id of ids) {
  const n = figma.getNodeById(id);
  if (!n) { out.push({id, error:'not found'}); continue; }
  const info = { id, name: n.name, type: n.type, x: n.x, y: n.y, w: n.width, h: n.height };
  if ('fills' in n) info.fills = n.fills.map(f => ({type:f.type, visible:f.visible, color: f.type==='SOLID'? f.color : undefined, image: f.type==='IMAGE'? {hash:f.imageHash, scale:f.scale?f.scaleMode...} : undefined, opacity: f.opacity}));
  if ('strokes' in n) info.strokes = n.strokes.map(s=>({type:s.type, color:s.type==='SOLID'?s.color:undefined}));
  if ('cornerRadius' in n) info.cornerRadius = n.cornerRadius;
  if ('characters' in n) info.text = n.characters; // for text
  if (n.type === 'COMPONENT' || n.type==='INSTANCE') info.children = n.children.map(c=>`${c.name}(${c.type}) id=${c.id}`);
  out.push(info);
}

```

The media nodes are NOT accessible via the plugin API at all — getNodeById returns missing, and walking the tree doesn't show them (only icons are there). This is strange. The metadata tool shows them (5:17 etc.), but the plugin API doesn't.

The sections 01-04 (images) are NOT in the tree.

This suggests that the image nodes exist in the file but the plugin sandbox doesn't include them... Actually no. More likely: the plugin's document tree may be a "visited" subtree — Figma plugin API getNodeById only works for nodes... hmm.

Actually the walk found 5:2 Media Library → 5:6 Body → 5:88 ICONS section and items. So walking DID descend into 5:6's children. But 5:14, 5:34, 5:52, 5:75 (sections 01-04) were not listed as children of 5:6. The walk only shows: 5:88 (05 ICONS). So in the plugin's data, the Media Library frame only contains the ICONS section?! But metadata shows all 5 sections.

Hmm wait — maybe the metadata `5:6` for Body is `x=0 y=176 w=1400 h=2000`. And the walk shows Body's children only include 5:88. That means plugin tree genuinely lacks those sections.

Unless... the file has unloaded content? Figma plugin API does lazy loading? No, plugin API loads entire document.

Hmm, could there be TWO pages with similar ids? The `figma.root.children` — pages listed: 0:1, 1:2, 1:3, 1:4, 49:2. I looked at page 1:4. Its child is 5:2 Media Library. OK.

But maybe the plugin connects to a DIFFERENT file? No — the fileKey is 1W2mMMjwk00S3IBRd9pKN9.

Wait, actually maybe the tool runs in a sandbox copy or some proxy where the file loaded is the same. Icons ARE accessible though, including 6:269 etc. which live under 5:90 under 5:88 under 5:6. So parts of the media page exist.

Hmm, interesting: what if walk returns only visible nodes for frames with certain property? No, walk returns everything.

What if the image sections (01-04) are hidden/off? They're at y offset: sections at y=252, 688, 1010, 1332 within Body; icons at 1590. All visible.

Could it be that the plugin host has permission restrictions where certain nodes are omitted? The metadata API (get_metadata) shows them. The screenshot tool can render them.

Alternative approach: copy these nodes using a different mechanism. 05:17 etc. aren't accessible via plugin. But get_screenshot CAN render a node — meaning the "read-only" API has access. But use_figma (write) can't reach them.

Hmm wait, let me re-check. Maybe I misidentified: `figma.getNodeById('5:17')` returned MISSING — but the metadata showed id 5:17 = Paradise_Group_Logo rounded-rectangle. Let me check ids again: metadata says 5:17 is the RECTANGLE with image fill named Paradise_Group_Logo inside tile 5:19, inside frame 5:18. And I walked 5:2 → children... but wait, maybe my walk DID include them but wanted names include 'Paradise_Group_Logo' which matched ONLY if visited. It didn't match → not visited.

Hmm, so the plugin tree genuinely doesn't have those nodes. Weird.

Possibility: The file is HUGE and the plugin sandbox truncates? Unlikely.

Possibility: This Figma MCP "use_figma" tool might run inside the Figma desktop app with a plugin that has access to the "current page" only?? But then how did walk find components page icons? I did `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` in the earlier async attempt that "succeeded silently"... Actually my earlier async main() set current page to Media and it "executed successfully" — maybe page changed. But then the sync walk found icons on Media page...

Actually wait, maybe the plugin sees the whole document. And the media images ARE there but... let me reconsider: In the first metadata dump filter, the walk found ids 5:91, 5:92, 6:269 etc. Those came from page 1:4. So the plugin has page 1:4 with frame 5:2 with only icons section visible.

Could the image sections live in nodes with a special "documentation" flag that the plugin API hides? I don't think so.

Hold on — maybe the metadata tool reported ids from a DIFFERENT file version (the READ-ONLY "source" file) while the plugin tool operates on... no, same fileKey.

Let me try: does getNodeById work for '5:2' (Media Library frame)? And check its children count. And try '5:6'. Also try walking with depth 0 from page to see all children of 5:2.

Also another approach: `figma.getNodeByIdAsync`? Not available. 

Alternative to get images: The images can be fetched if I know imageHash — but I can't read fills of nodes I can't access. However, the metadata tool (read-only) DOES know fills? get_metadata only returns structure, not fills.

Hmm, what about get_design_context? The instructions mention "get_design_context" tool — but I don't have it in my toolset! The metadata output says "IMPORTANT: After you call this tool, you MUST call get_design_context if trying to implement the design". But my available tools are only: get_screenshot, get_metadata, whoami, use_figma. There's no get_design_context tool exposed. OK.

So how do I get the media images into the workspace?

Option A: get_screenshot on media asset nodes → get PNG bytes → but I cannot upload images into the file (createImageAsync not supported per gotchas: "MUST NEVER use ... createImageAsync"). Hmm. But maybe I can insert the image via... no.

Wait — the media assets are raster images inside the file. They have imageHashes stored in the file. If I could read the imageHash from the fills, I could apply the same fill to a new rectangle (fill with the SAME imageHash — no upload needed!). That's the standard trick: copy image fill by reference. But I can't access the nodes to read their fills...

Unless the plugin CAN access them but only on a different page? Let me try getNodeById variants and a fresh full-document walk with explicit count of nodes, printing total children counts at each level to see what's missing.

Another thought: maybe those nodes exist under a page that is NOT in figma.root.children (e.g., a "local" component?), no.

Let me also try: `figma.getNodeById('5:14')` returned MISSING — maybe because node ids with pattern like 5:14 are not loadable for image fills? No...

Hmm, actually — wait. Let me reconsider the earlier async function: `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` — did it succeed? The result was "执行成功" but no output. Actually the FIRST async call (the one with walk of components) also succeeded without output — because maybe async functions' throw gets swallowed silently by the harness (the tool just logs 执行成功 without capturing the promise rejection). The sync throw works.

So my sync walk result above IS accurate: plugin sees only icons sections on Media page.

Wait, actually — maybe the plugin's walk DID stop early because of depth limit (8). Sections 01-04 are at depth: page(0) → 5:2(1) → 5:6(2) → 5:14(3) → 5:16(4) → 5:18(5) → 5:19(6) → 5:17(7). Depth <= 8, fine.

And 5:88 icons: page(0) → 5:2(1) → 5:6(2) → 5:88(3). We saw 5:88 at depth 3 in output. Then 5:90 (4), 5:91 (5), 5:92 (6), 6:269 (7), 4:49 (8). OK.

So sections 5:14, 5:34, 5:52, 5:75 are NOT children of 5:6 in plugin view. But metadata shows 5:6 Body with children 5:7 (Media Guide), 5:14, ...

Actually hold on — maybe the plugin view and the metadata view show different LAYERS. Maybe in the current file, the media page '04 · Media 素材库' has TWO frames: Media Library (5:2) that plugin sees, and... no.

Let me check the Components page more carefully — maybe the button/text field components there reference images... not needed.

Alternatively, maybe the plugin is scoped to a "draft" copy of the doc that excludes pages except current? No.

OK here's another possibility that makes sense: The use_figma plugin might run against the LIVE file but its document only contains nodes reachable from... hmm.

Simplest robust approach: copy node by reference via the REST-ish APIs? Not available.

Wait — actually! There might be a much simpler explanation: use_figma tool might run in the FIGMA DESKTOP APP with the plugin loaded into the CURRENT FILE but the plugin's file loading might be LIMITED to what's been "opened" — Figma loads the whole file though.

Let me just try re-walking the media page but printing children of 5:2 and 5:6 explicitly to confirm.

Actually, let me try a totally different approach: maybe the walk hit a "hidden" node filter? Let me print ALL children (id+name+type) of 5:2 with full depth and no name filter.

messages.reasoning_content:
Interesting! The Media Library frame only has ONE child: "5:6:Body" — and Body only has one child: "5:88:05 ICONS (VECTOR)". So in the actual file, ALL the media image sections (brand, illustration, avatar, coins, articles, notifications, bank logos) are MISSING from the live document! Only the ICONS section exists.

Wait — but the metadata dump from get_metadata showed all those sections: 5:6 Body with children 5:7 Media Guide, 5:14 01 BRAND & ILLUSTRATION, 5:34 02 INVESTMENT PLANS, 5:52 03 CONTENT IMAGES, 5:75 04 BANK LOGOS, 5:88 05 ICONS (VECTOR).

Hmm, that's inconsistent. The get_metadata tool (which reads via the Figma REST API presumably) shows all sections, but the plugin (which loads the file into the desktop app) only shows the icons section. This could be a caching issue: the plugin may have loaded a stale/partial document. OR the desktop app session loads only some nodes.

Wait, actually maybe the plugin's figma document was loaded at session start and the sections were added later (could be that the file was being edited). But the REST metadata showed them...

Let me try re-reading: maybe the plugin needs a fresh load. I can't force reload within a plugin.

Alternative: The Figma REST API (get_design_context) might be able to access those nodes. But get_design_context is a read-only tool. Can I get the image contents? The task says use use_figma to build; do I have a way to import images?

Options for images:
1. Figma Plugin API `figma.createImageAsync` — explicitly listed as NEVER use, not supported.
2. `figma.getNodeById` — only returns nodes in the loaded document.
3. REST API GET /v1/images — not available as a tool.
4. `get_screenshot` — can render nodes, but not for getting image data into the file.

Hmm wait — but actually, maybe the plugin CAN see the media sections if I look at the icons page... Let me reconsider. The dump of page 1:4 showed pageChildren only [5:2 Media Library]. And Media Library childIds only ["5:6:Body"], Body childIds only ["5:88:05  ICONS (VECTOR)"]. So within the plugin's loaded document, ONLY the icons exist? But wait the icons are components that are referenced from 02 Components page (6:269 etc. are in page 1:3). Actually 5:88 is in the media page and references symbols from 1:3.

Hmm, hold on. Maybe the sections exist but the walk failed because... childIds showed just 5:6:Body for 5:2. That's definitive — in the plugin view, Body has ONE child.

But get_metadata (REST) shows Body with children 5:7, 5:14, 5:34, 5:52, 5:75, 5:88. That's the file's actual state.

So there's a mismatch: the REST API sees the full file; the plugin (desktop app) sees only a partial tree. This might be a "collapsed" loading behavior in the desktop app — no, children arrays would still be complete.

Actually — wait. Maybe I should re-run the sync walk of page 1:4 to confirm what the plugin sees. The first walk earlier ("Dump full tree of Media Library page") — the output was truncated/hidden ("历史结果已压缩"). The second probe confirmed childIds ["5:6:Body"] etc.

Hmm, could it be that the desktop app has the file open with old cached version and the media assets were added by the benchmark harness AFTER the app cached? But then REST would also be cached...

Actually the metadata tool results for 1:4 showed the full tree, and I obtained that AFTER the session started. The first use_figma tree dump of media page ALSO should have been after. Let me re-dump the media page tree once more carefully — full child names at each level to see what's there now. Maybe there was a transient state.

Alternatively, maybe get_design_context can fetch the file structure for media nodes, and I can then reference asset images via the REST Image API — but there's no REST tool for images.

Wait — is there any tool that can generate image bytes and put them into Figma? get_screenshot generates PNGs of nodes, with base64 optional. But that renders the DESIGN VIEW, not raw image bytes, and doesn't help create image fills in the plugin.

Hmm, but actually, maybe I don't need the exact raster assets. The brief says media should be reused ("If 04 · Media is present, read and reuse its assets too"). The media library sections ARE present per REST metadata. The plugin can't see them, which is a tooling limitation.

Let me try once more — perhaps re-querying the file reloads the plugin document. Actually each use_figma call might run in the same plugin session. Let me try dumping the WHOLE document tree (root children) to see what the plugin sees globally.

Actually I realize my earlier full-tree walks only recorded found items for wanted names in the media page... no wait, the probe clearly showed the structure. Let me do one comprehensive document-level dump of what the plugin sees: pages and their top frames with child count. Then decide.

Also note: get_design_context for node 5:2 might give me REST-level structure with details for the media frames including their fills (imageHash). If I know the imageHash, can I set an image fill? No — createImageAsync is banned, and there's no API to create a fill from a hash.

Hmm, actually wait: is there a way to clone nodes within the plugin? If the plugin can't see the nodes, no.

BUT maybe I can access them via the REST API using figma.getNodeById? No, that's plugin-side.

The get_design_context tool — let me call it for node 5:2 to see if there's richer info (like image refs or URLs). It returns XML metadata — same as get_metadata probably, but "preferred". Let me call get_design_context on the media frame and on the Components page to learn everything about the icons (paths as vector data?) — actually metadata doesn't include vector paths usually.

OK here's the thing: for icons, they're COMPONENTS (6:269 etc). The plugin can see them (they're on the Components page). I can clone them with figma.createInstance or importComponentById? There's figma.importComponentByKeyAsync — banned? No, only loadAllPagesAsync, setPluginData, createImageAsync are banned. importComponentByKeyAsync is allowed but needs component keys. I can get keys by reading component node .key in the plugin.

So: icons + button + textfield + shell are all accessible as components in the plugin (they live on Components page). Media images are NOT accessible in the plugin view.

So for media assets (which are raster images displayed via image fills), options:
1. Clone via plugin → impossible if not visible.
2. Use get_design_context to obtain image fill URLs? REST metadata may include imageRef but not URL. No tool to fetch images into the file.
3. Substitute with drawn placeholders? The brief says media reuse is expected; the media guide says "Raster images keep their original bytes; use Fit for logos and coins..." If the plugin can't access them, I could try harder.

Wait — maybe the plugin CAN see them but my walk had a bug: `if ('children' in n) for (const c of n.children) walk(c, path);` with path as array — fine. But probe used n.children directly on 5:2 and 5:6 — definitive.

Hmm, could the desktop app version of the plugin API return cached children while getNodeById for deep nodes fails because they're not loaded? In Figma desktop, all nodes in the document ARE loaded. Unless the file uses "linked" content... no.

Actually — thinking about it — maybe the harness created the file with those sections but the plugin session operates on a REDUCED COPY of the file (the benchmark might strip media to test fallback?) — no, that seems wrong.

Let me just try get_design_context on 5:2 and see if it shows the sections (read-only REST view). If REST shows them, I'll try the plugin a couple more times (e.g., switch current page away and back, or use figma.getNodeById on the section frame IDs from REST). If the plugin still can't see them, I'll proceed by RE-CREATING equivalent placeholder imagery for media (since media content can't be extracted), while reusing everything else (icons, components, shell) from the library.

Actually wait — one more idea: figma.getNodeById might return nodes from OTHER pages if they're in the loaded doc; the Media page in the loaded doc might genuinely only contain icons. Perhaps the harness intends exactly this: "04 · Media 素材库" page exists, contains what it contains. The sections I saw in REST metadata (get_metadata) might be... hmm, but get_metadata showed them.

Let me call get_design_context on 1:4 now (REST-based) to double-check the REST view, and also dump plugin view of pages again. Compare. Then decide.

```js
function text(str, x, y, size, opts={}) {
  const t = figma.createText();
  t.characters = str;
  t.fontName = { family: opts.family||'Inter', style: opts.style||'Regular' };
  t.fontSize = size;
  t.fills = [solid(opts.color||T.ink)];
  t.x = x; t.y = y;
  if (opts.width !== undefined) { t.textAutoResize = 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'; t.resize(opts.width, t.height); t.textAutoResize = 'HEIGHT'; }
  if (opts.letterSpacing !== undefined) t.letterSpacing = { value: opts.letterSpacing, unit: 'PIXELS' };
  if (opts.lineHeight !== undefined) t.lineHeight = { value: opts.lineHeight, unit: 'PIXELS' };
  return t;
}
```

```js
function rect(x,y,w,h, fill, r=0, opts={}) {
  const n = figma.createRectangle();
  n.x=x; n.y=y; n.resize(w,h);
  n.fills = fill ? [solid(fill)] : [];
  if (r) n.cornerRadius = r;
  if (opts.stroke) { n.strokes=[solid(opts.stroke)]; n.strokeWeight=opts.strokeWeight||1; }
  if (opts.strokeAlign) n.strokeAlign=opts.strokeAlign;
  return n;
}
```

```js
function frame(name, x, y, w, h, opts={}) {

}
```

```js
}
```

```js
function img(parent, srcClone, x, y, w, h, rad=0, mode='COVER') {
  const c = srcClone.clone();

  c.fills = c.fills.map(f => f.type==='IMAGE' ? {...f, scaleMode: mode} : f);
```

function.name: mcp__figma__get_screenshot
function.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`. Only set `enableBase64Response: true` when the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests); when set, an inline base64 image entry is appended to the response in addition to the URL and curl instructions. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

sessionId.description: After create_session succeeds, pass its exact returned UUID here on every file-tool call for this task, even when fileKey differs.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

contentsOnly.description: When true, renders the node in isolation — floating/overlapping content (e.g. connectors parented to the page that visually sit above a section) is excluded. Defaults to false so screenshots match what the user sees on the canvas. Only set to true if the caller specifically needs the isolated render.

enableBase64Response.description: When true, the response also includes the screenshot inline as a base64-encoded image entry, in addition to the short-lived URL and curl instructions. Defaults to false. Set to true ONLY if the agent cannot fetch URLs (no shell access, no HTTP client, or a sandboxed environment that blocks outbound requests)

maxDimension.description: Optional. Maximum pixel size of the longer edge of the rendered screenshot — the server scales the node so that max(width, height) ≤ maxDimension while preserving aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024. Must be a positive integer; values above 65536 are rejected. Increase when the agent will visually inspect fine detail; decrease for thumbnails or to save context.

function.name: mcp__figma__get_metadata
function.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

function.name: mcp__figma__use_figma
function.description:
Create, edit, generate, or sync any design in Figma — UIs, screens, mockups, components, frames, variables, styles, text, images, layouts, and design systems. This general-purpose tool writes to Figma with JavaScript via the Figma Plugin API. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`).

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, load figma-use guidance — prefer the /figma-use skill if available, otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md MCP resource if available. Skipping this causes common, hard-to-debug failures.

Use this tool when the user wants to:
- Create or generate a Figma design, screen, UI, or mockup from scratch, intent, or code
- Update, edit, or sync an existing Figma design
- Generate or sync Figma designs from source code
- Set up or modify design tokens, variables, or styles
- Build or extend a design system or component/variant library
- Fix layout, spacing, auto-layout, or fill/hug issues
- Add component descriptions, annotations and Code Connect metadata to nodes
- Review or fix accessibility, contrast, typography, or visual polish
- Inspect or query node properties programmatically
CHOOSING BETWEEN use_figma AND generate_figma_design:
- Default to use_figma for all write operations
- Exception: generate_figma_design ONLY to capture a web app page/view for the first time. For web apps, run both in parallel — generate_figma_design captures a pixel-perfect screenshot, use_figma builds from imported design system components and refines against the screenshot
- Non-web (iOS, Android, generic UI) and from-scratch designs: use_figma only
- Updating/syncing a Figma page already captured: use_figma — even if source code changed
GOTCHAS
- For the font "Inter", the style is "Semi Bold", not "SemiBold" and "Extra Bold" not "ExtraBold"
- MUST use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to change pages. Setting figma.currentPage is not supported
- MUST NEVER use loadAllPagesAsync,setPluginData,createImageAsync. They are not supported API
